Without a pre-existing structure, you may need to be more intentional and reflective about what truly matters to you. This can provide a clear sense of direction and help them prioritize their time and energy. However, without such a framework, you may need to rely more on your own values, goals, and personal reflections to guide your decisions. This can be both a challenge and an opportunity. On one hand, you may need to put in more effort to discover what truly matters to you and what brings you a sense of purpose and fulfillment. On the other hand, you have the freedom to create your own meaning and priorities, unencumbered by external expectations or traditions. To figure out what's worth your time, you may need to engage in more self-reflection and exploration. By taking the time to reflect on these questions and explore your own values and priorities, you can create a personalized framework for deciding what's worth your time and energy. This may involve setting personal goals, prioritizing relationships and activities that bring you joy, and being mindful of how you allocate your time and attention. Ultimately, not having a traditional religious or cultural framework can be a liberating experience, allowing you to create your own path and priorities.
